wSF82AwSDiU.summary: Gary Wilson's TEDxGlasgow talk argues that internet pornography hyperstimulates the brain's reward system and can cause symptoms that reverse when people stop. TED notes that several claims are not supported by respected academic studies.
wSF82AwSDiU.why: HN commenters frequently recommend it as an eye-opening case against heavy porn use, though it is contested science.

wjZofJX0v4M.summary: 3Blue1Brown's visual explanation of how transformers and GPT-style language models work, tracing data through tokens, embeddings and attention.
wjZofJX0v4M.why: HN treats it as the go-to visual introduction to transformers, and many say it finally made attention and embeddings click.

wbSwFU6tY1c.summary: SpaceX's livestream of the Falcon Heavy test flight, including the launch, side booster landings and Tesla Roadster payload. It was the first launch of the most powerful operational rocket at the time.
wbSwFU6tY1c.why: HN commenters cite it as a landmark launch broadcast, and also dissect details like the duplicated booster landing feeds.

wfm2xCKOCNk.summary: A video explaining why Japanese cities look the way they do, through Japan's national tiered zoning system that permits mixed use and flexible development. It compares this approach with more restrictive zoning elsewhere.
wfm2xCKOCNk.why: HN commenters recommend it as the go-to explanation of Japanese zoning in housing and urbanism debates.

wh4aWZRtTwU.summary: Technology Connections explains why brown is not a spectral color but a context-dependent perception, essentially dark orange seen against brighter surroundings.
wh4aWZRtTwU.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a surprisingly magical explainer on color perception, often cited in color-space discussions.

wlR5gYd6um0.summary: Chris Toomey of thoughtbot explains Vim as a language of commands, motions and text objects that combine into precise edits. He shows how to master the built-in pieces and extend them.
wlR5gYd6um0.why: Repeatedly called the best video introduction to Vim's underlying model.

wo84LFzx5nI.summary: Casey Muratori's two-hour talk tracing the history of object-oriented programming back to the 1960s and examining how its ideas, and later entity component systems, came about. It is followed by a Q&A.
wo84LFzx5nI.why: HN commenters recommend it for its source-based history of OOP, though some dispute its account of Alan Kay.

wt-iVFxgFWk.summary: John Carmack's long QuakeCon 2012 keynote, a free-ranging talk covering software engineering, game platforms, game streaming, and his early head-mounted display and VR work.
wt-iVFxgFWk.why: HN rates his QuakeCon keynotes among the best technical talks, and cites this one for the VR segment and for his views on Linux gaming.

w3_0x6oaDmI.summary: Tom Scott explains for Computerphile why electronic voting is a bad idea, arguing that paper ballots are transparent, auditable and hard to tamper with at scale. He covers why moving voting to phones, tablets or computers undermines trust and verifiability.
w3_0x6oaDmI.why: It is the go-to short explainer HN commenters link whenever e-voting, voting machines or online voting come up.

wfYbgdo8e-8.summary: CGP Grey explains split-brain patients, where severing the corpus callosum lets the two hemispheres act independently. He uses this to explore the idea of two minds in one head.
wfYbgdo8e-8.why: HN returns to it constantly in consciousness and decision-making threads as a clear, entertaining explanation of split-brain.

wrwgIjBUYVc.summary: ScienceClic explains why the rubber sheet analogy for general relativity is misleading and offers a new visualization that includes the curvature of time and shows gravity as motion through curved spacetime.
wrwgIjBUYVc.why: Called the best visualization of general relativity by many commenters, who say it cleared up long-held misunderstandings of gravity.

wupToqz1e2g.summary: Carl Sagan's narration of the Pale Blue Dot passage, reflecting on the Voyager photograph of Earth as a tiny speck in space. It is a short meditation on humanity's smallness and shared home.
wupToqz1e2g.why: HN commenters return to it for perspective, comfort and Sagan's soothing voice, and suggest watching it periodically.

wxL4ElboiuA.summary: Dalibor Farny documents the hand manufacture of a nixie tube, from glassblowing to evacuation, with text notes rather than narration. He revived the lost craft of nixie tube making.
wxL4ElboiuA.why: HN commenters call it mesmerizing and a great look at how things are actually made by a dedicated craftsman.

wdgULBpRoXk.summary: Ben Eater explains how a USB keyboard communicates, covering the electrical interface, bit and packet encoding, packet contents, and a comparison with PS/2.
wdgULBpRoXk.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, comprehensive explanation of USB signaling and keyboard polling.

wqn3gR1WTcA.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment explains how data brokers collect and sell personal information, including a stunt in which his team bought data to identify members of Congress.
wqn3gR1WTcA.why: HN recommends it as an accessible overview of the data broker industry in privacy discussions.

w3WYdYyjek4.summary: Joran Dirk Greef's Systems Distributed '23 talk on TigerStyle, the engineering methodology behind TigerBeetle. It covers designing safer systems in less time through up-front design, assertions, and deterministic simulation.
w3WYdYyjek4.why: HN commenters, including TigerBeetle people, recommend it as the explanation of a methodology for building defect-free, high-assurance software.

wGt4XwBbCvA.summary: Jean-Marc Jancovici lectures at ENS Paris on whether energy use, jobs and growth can all be preserved. He argues for a physical approach to economics, since resource depletion and climate limits make perpetual GDP growth unrealistic.
wGt4XwBbCvA.why: Recommended as a sober, physics-based account of how energy underlies the economy.

wJyUtbn0O5Y.summary: An award-winning 3D animation by XVIVO for Harvard's BioVisions showing the molecular machinery inside a cell as a white blood cell responds to a stimulus.
wJyUtbn0O5Y.why: Recommended as a jaw-dropping view of the complexity and machine-like nature of cells.

wJWksPWDKOc.summary: The complete six-stage album series Everywhere at the End of Time by The Caretaker, about 6.5 hours of music that depicts the progression of dementia through distorted, decaying old ballroom recordings.
wJWksPWDKOc.why: HN recommends it, often emotionally, as an auditory depiction of memory loss, in threads about dementia and aging.

wM8Xli2KTzI.summary: FortNine argues that e-bikes have injury rates and speeds closer to motorcycles than to pedal bikes. It argues riders should treat them with similar safety gear and caution.
wM8Xli2KTzI.why: Cited repeatedly in e-bike threads as a well-argued safety counterpoint from someone who rides both.

whPWKecazgM.summary: Ian Hubert's Blender Conference talk on world building in Blender, covering photogrammetry, camera projection and assembling complex environments from simple shapes at great speed.
whPWKecazgM.why: HN considers it a fantastic, mind-blowing talk that shows how a single skilled artist can build detailed VFX scenes quickly.

wAIP6fI0NAI.summary: Jon Ronson's TED talk on public shaming on Twitter, centered on Justine Sacco and others whose lives were upended by online mobs. He argues we have become a baying crowd and should rethink how we treat each other online.
wAIP6fI0NAI.why: HN commenters bring it up in threads about online mobs and cancellation as a relevant talk by a journalist who interviewed shamed people.

wpOxbesRNBc.summary: David MacKay's 2007 Google Tech Talk presents Dasher, a text-entry system driven by continuous gestures and a language model, reaching about 35 words per minute with one finger and 25 hands-free. It explains the information-theory reasoning behind the design.
wpOxbesRNBc.why: Regarded as the seminal talk on Dasher, recommended in threads on accessible and alternative text input.

wsaufB5F8dk.summary: Dr. Bruce Bugbee walks through the calculations for crop yield potential when light is the limiting factor, from photosynthetic quantum yield through respiration efficiency and harvest index, using the Energy Cascade Model.
wsaufB5F8dk.why: Cited in vertical farming debates as a rigorous look at when indoor crops are economically viable.

wtV5ev6813I.summary: Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen explains in a TEDx talk why Germany has lower crime and far fewer prisoners than the US, and what American criminal justice could learn from German prisons.
wtV5ev6813I.why: HN recommends it as a comparison of German rehabilitative prisons with American retributive justice, backed by statistics.

wASCH_gPnDw.summary: A Channel 9 Going Deep interview in which Brian Beckman talks with Rich Hickey, creator of Clojure, about the language's design. It covers Clojure's persistent data structures, reference types and its approach to concurrency on the JVM.
wASCH_gPnDw.why: HN commenters call it a fantastic introduction to Clojure and the thinking behind its design.

wFpeM3fxJoQ.summary: A timelapse compilation of the night sky above the Very Large Telescope at Paranal, Chile, using ESO photographers' footage set to music. It shows the stars wheeling overhead and the observatory at work.
wFpeM3fxJoQ.why: Commenters recommend it as an awe-inspiring way to feel Earth's rotation and our place in space.

wSdV1M7n4gQ.summary: Anders Hejlsberg whiteboards how compilers are taught versus how modern ones are actually built. He explains the shift to compilers as services with incremental, error-tolerant, IDE-oriented design, as in Roslyn and TypeScript.
wSdV1M7n4gQ.why: It is the standard reference for why modern compilers and language servers differ from textbook designs, cited in rust-analyzer and parsing threads.

wqu_IpkOYBg.summary: Debris by Farbrausch, the winner of the Breakpoint 2007 demo competition. All of its 3D visuals, textures and music come from a single 177 KB executable.
wqu_IpkOYBg.why: HN recommends it as the demoscene showpiece to show someone what extreme size-limited real-time graphics look like.

wE5G1kTndI4.summary: CityNerd lays out a data-driven method for deciding where high-speed rail should be built in North America and identifies 56 city pairs that justify it, based on population and distance.
wE5G1kTndI4.why: HN recommends it as a methodical argument that many US city pairs make economic sense for high-speed rail.

wICOlaQOpM0.summary: PBS Space Time examines the interstellar object 'Oumuamua and the popular theories about it, including the light-sail hypothesis. It argues that a natural rock is the likeliest explanation.
wICOlaQOpM0.why: HN recommends it as a sober analysis of 'Oumuamua theories that counters the alien-spacecraft claims.

wVp5koAOu9M.summary: Kirsten Dirksen tours new Earthships, homes built from tires, bottles and cans that generate their own energy, collect water and grow food. The video covers the newer, cheaper Encounter model and its passive systems.
wVp5koAOu9M.why: HN commenters recommend the channel's alternative-living videos, and this one for its look at a net-zero desert home.

whb4unrhy44.summary: Maggie Mae Fish analyzes the documentary My Octopus Teacher as an eco-horror film, critiquing it as a story of a man projecting his own needs onto a wild animal.
whb4unrhy44.why: HN recommends it as a well-done critique of the documentary, sometimes in preference to watching the film itself.

wwmOkaKh3-s.summary: Charlie Rose interviews Sir James Goldsmith in 1994 about the coming GATT free-trade agreement. Goldsmith predicts that global capital mobility will upset the balance between capital and labor.
wwmOkaKh3-s.why: Recommended as a prescient interview on free trade and its social consequences, worth watching with hindsight.

w70Xc9CStoE.summary: Ross Scott of Accursed Farms lays out a campaign to stop publishers from permanently shutting down games, using The Crew as the test case. He covers government initiatives and the legal options, and the stopkillinggames.com site.
w70Xc9CStoE.why: HN points to it as the original statement of the Stop Killing Games campaign.

wOmjnioNulo.summary: CGP Grey explains why horses could be ridden and why other animals like zebras and bears were never domesticated for war or riding. It is a follow-up on the topic of animal domestication.
wOmjnioNulo.why: HN recommends it as a classic on why some animals are suited to farming and domestication and others are not.

wTPGW1PNy_Y.summary: Lukas Eder's Devoxx talk on how modern cost-based SQL optimizers rewrite and plan queries in ways developers would not expect. It argues that declarative SQL, used well, can run complex queries very fast.
wTPGW1PNy_Y.why: HN commenters recommend it to developers unfamiliar with how much leverage and intelligence there is in a SQL database.

wUwZZaI5u0c.summary: PBS Infinite Series explains how Shor's algorithm lets a quantum computer break RSA encryption, building on earlier episodes about cryptography and the math of quantum computers. It works through the idea step by step.
wUwZZaI5u0c.why: HN recommends it as a clear, worked explanation of Shor's algorithm for building intuition.

w_znRopGtbE.summary: Jeri Ellsworth shows step by step how to make an NMOS transistor at home using a kiln, rust remover, spin-on dopant, eBay wafers and vinyl stickers.
w_znRopGtbE.why: HN points to it as the classic example of home-made semiconductors and a fun way to go down to the transistor level.

wcBEOcPtlYk.summary: Guitarist Jim Lill spends a year testing where guitar amplifier tone comes from, swapping tubes, rectifiers and bias types. He finds that much of it can be reproduced with EQ and distortion in different orders.
wcBEOcPtlYk.why: Recommended as a systematic, surprising experiment, often cited in audio and gear-obsession threads.

wlvKAT7SZIQ.summary: Daniel Lemire's QCon talk on how simdjson parses gigabytes of JSON per second. It covers SIMD vectorization, branch prediction and the lessons learned building a fast parser.
wlvKAT7SZIQ.why: HN points to it as the best explanation of simdjson internals and of why fast parsing is rarely disk-bound.

wtIhVwPruwY.summary: Numberphile with Tom Crawford of Oxford explains the Reynolds number, the second of three videos on Navier-Stokes and fluid flow, with demonstrations of laminar versus turbulent behavior.
wtIhVwPruwY.why: HN recommends it as an accessible layperson's introduction to the Reynolds number and fluid dynamics scales.

wvJaKQ94lBY.summary: An overview of the PTVS 2.0 beta feature for debugging Python and C/C++ together in one session in Visual Studio.
wvJaKQ94lBY.why: Linked whenever mixed Python and C++ debugging came up as a neat PTVS feature.

w-I6XTVZXww.summary: A Numberphile video in which physicists Tony Padilla and Ed Copeland show a seemingly astounding result that 1+2+3+4+... equals -1/12. The argument is informal and has drawn criticism for glossing over what the result actually means.
w-I6XTVZXww.why: HN uses it as the standard reference for the -1/12 meme, with commenters split between enjoying it and calling it a cheat.

wMFPe-DwULM.summary: A clip from the BBC Fun to Imagine series in which Richard Feynman is asked how magnets work and explains why 'why' questions depend on a shared framework of understanding and cannot always be answered in layman's terms.
wMFPe-DwULM.why: Cited constantly when discussing explaining to non-experts, the limits of explanation and what a 'why' question really asks.

wO2lWmgEK1Y.summary: A Financial Times film examining how Brexit hurt the UK economy, with FT writers and business people. It looks at trade effects, political silence about the costs, and the absence of a convincing Brexit dividend.
wO2lWmgEK1Y.why: Pointed to as an in-depth, journalistic account of Brexit's economic aftermath.

wROQUZDCIMI.summary: Moon Channel, run by a lawyer, explains the legal basis for emulation, including the history of emulation case law and Nintendo's takedown of Dolphin's Steam release. It argues the legality of emulators is more fragile than most people assume.
wROQUZDCIMI.why: HN points to it as a clear, lawyer-made summary during Nintendo emulator disputes like Yuzu.

wfzSE4Hoxbc.summary: A 2015 talk by David Deutsch with slides and audio about constructor theory and how physics, in particular the many-worlds interpretation, can be framed without probability.
wfzSE4Hoxbc.why: Cited in threads on probability and quantum theory as a strong argument that probabilities can be eliminated from physics.

wq5D43qAsVg.summary: Part 3 of Kirby Ferguson's Everything is a Remix series, using Apple and the iPhone to show how invention builds on copying and combining prior ideas. It argues that creativity and innovation are inseparable from copying.
wq5D43qAsVg.why: Cited in copyright and patent debates to argue that creative works and inventions evolve by building on earlier ones.

w2A8q3XIhu0.summary: Tom Scott explains why hold music sounds worse than it used to, tracing it to old telephone exchanges and the audio compression applied by modern switches. It is a short visit to the Milton Keynes Museum.
w2A8q3XIhu0.why: HN links it as the standard answer to why phone hold music sounds poor.

wBBnfu8N_J0.summary: Physicist Angela Collier uses Gell-Mann amnesia to critique pop-science figures, especially Michio Kaku, and works through an eigenvalue problem along the way. It is a long, rambling commentary on how experts see simplified explanations of their own field.
wBBnfu8N_J0.why: HN commenters recommend it for the Gell-Mann amnesia framing and as a skeptical take on Michio Kaku.

wIC-iGDTU40.summary: A Technology Connections video weighing LED streetlights against high pressure sodium lamps, covering efficiency, color, cost and light pollution. It is a follow-up to his earlier explanation of why street lights are orange.
wIC-iGDTU40.why: HN commenters point to it in lighting threads for its pros and cons of LED versus sodium lamps, though one calls it almost right.

wK5v1Nw98xs.summary: A roughly three-hour technical livestream Q&A on Helion Energy's fusion approach and the National Ignition Facility. It covers neutron production, shielding, energy recovery, diagnostics and why tokamaks might fare better.
wK5v1Nw98xs.why: HN commenters cite it as a detailed critical counterpoint to Helion's claims, for those who want more than the hype.

wOlcB-JxkFw.summary: Alexander Bruce's GDC talk on making Antichamber, from working alone in a bedroom to winning acclaim at the IGF. It focuses on the psychological challenge of seven years of solo development.
wOlcB-JxkFw.why: HN commenters recommend it as an honest account of the emotional toll and persistence of long indie game development.

wW9CAH9nSLs.summary: Solomon Hykes shows Docker to the public for the first time in a five-minute lightning talk at PyCon 2013. It demos Linux containers and the simplicity of a Dockerfile.
wW9CAH9nSLs.why: HN commenters point to it as the historic first Docker demo and a quick overview of what Docker is.

wbp-3BJWsU8.summary: Josh Bloch and Jeremy Manson present the eighth installment of Java Puzzlers at Google I/O 2011, a set of surprising corner cases in the Java language and libraries. It includes puzzlers on traps such as regular expression performance.
wbp-3BJWsU8.why: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining tour of exotic Java corner cases.

wgHIkdUQbp0.summary: The first episode of a long live-coding series in which Immo Landwerth builds the Minsk compiler for a small language in C#. It starts with a basic expression evaluator and builds toward a full language.
wgHIkdUQbp0.why: Recommended as a practical, approachable build-it-step-by-step introduction to writing compilers, light on theory.

wCEkK1YzqBo.summary: WSJ's Joanna Stern interviews Apple's Craig Federighi and Greg Joswiak at WWDC 2025 about Siri's delays, AI strategy, the Liquid Glass redesign in iOS 26, iPad versus Mac, and tariffs.
wCEkK1YzqBo.why: Commenters cite it as a rare, pointed grilling of Apple executives over why Siri fell behind.

wg6cfsnmqyg.summary: An excerpt from Russell Barkley's lecture on ADHD, focusing on inhibition, impulsivity and emotional regulation. It explains ADHD as a problem of response inhibition and emotional impulsivity.
wg6cfsnmqyg.why: HN commenters point to Barkley's talks as a respected clinician's view of ADHD as a spectrum of executive function problems.

ws3DJF7MbMU.summary: Part 1 of a documentary on the Commodore Amiga, from the Lorraine prototype and the Atari and Commodore buyouts through the Amiga 1000 launch in the 1980s.
ws3DJF7MbMU.why: Recommended as a wonderful, thorough telling of the Amiga story in threads about the machine.

wvfR3XLXPvw.summary: A short PBS Eons episode on carcinization, the repeated independent evolution of crab-like bodies in unrelated crustaceans, and what makes that form so successful.
wvfR3XLXPvw.why: HN cites it as a clear, well-made treatment of convergent evolution and crabs.

wzFhBGKU6HA.summary: A 2006 IBM commercial depicting a future supermarket where shoppers walk out and RFID automatically charges them for their items.
wzFhBGKU6HA.why: HN commenters cite it as proof that walk-out shopping was envisioned long before Amazon's version, and as an appealing vision of the future.

w-WMn_zHCVo.summary: A driver films a police DUI checkpoint on the 4th of July where a drug dog alerts on his car and he is searched without consent, though he broke no laws. He is released without charges after officers learn he was recording.
w-WMn_zHCVo.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of police cueing drug dogs to justify searches.

w-tFdreZB94.summary: Microsoft's 2015 concept video imagining how ubiquitous computing, collaboration services and data analytics might change work 5-10 years later.
w-tFdreZB94.why: Cited as an example of corporate future-concept videos, sometimes appreciated for its ideas and sometimes used as a cautionary comparison.

w5ebcowAJD8.summary: Veritasium builds a QR code by hand to explain how it works. It covers the history of Morse code and barcodes, how QR codes encode data, why damaged codes still scan, and how safe they are.
w5ebcowAJD8.why: HN points to it as a recent, well-made explanation of QR code structure and error correction.

w8J5BWL8oJY.summary: A surreal multimedia TEDxSarasota performance by Magic Leap founder Rony Abovitz, held on 12/12/12, mixing performance art with talk about imagination and creativity.
w8J5BWL8oJY.why: Mostly cited as damning evidence of Magic Leap's hype and marketing, with commenters calling it delusional or a fraud signal.

w8c_m6U1f9o.summary: A satirical Onion Talks episode in which a startup founder explains making money by selling his users' data to oppressive governments. It parodies tech conference talks and monetization of communities.
w8c_m6U1f9o.why: Posted as a joke or satire whenever a company sells out its users or surveillance comes up.

wKISPePFrIs.summary: Saqib Shaikh, a blind developer at Microsoft, shows at Build 2017 how he writes and debugs code in Visual Studio using a screen reader. This version adds subtitles.
wKISPePFrIs.why: HN uses it as the go-to example of how blind developers work, including the very fast screen reader speech.

wTjMqda19wk.summary: The opening scene of HBO's The Newsroom, in which anchor Will McAvoy answers a student's question about why America is the greatest country. He delivers a blunt speech arguing it no longer is.
wTjMqda19wk.why: Posted in threads on US costs and institutions as a famous fictional rebuttal to American exceptionalism.

wW5vJyI_HcU.summary: Brian Krebs and Lance James present research on DDoS booter services at Black Hat 2013, including the SWATting Krebs suffered. HN knows it mainly for a later exchange between Krebs and Cloudflare's Matthew Prince.
wW5vJyI_HcU.why: Mostly cited as the source of the Krebs critique of Cloudflare and Prince's onstage response, which commenters debate.

wgSZA3NPpBs.summary: The 2016 Isaac Asimov Memorial Debate, moderated by Neil deGrasse Tyson, in which a panel of physicists and philosophers debates whether the universe is a simulation. Participants include David Chalmers, Zohreh Davoudi and James Gates.
wgSZA3NPpBs.why: Linked in simulation-hypothesis threads as an expert panel that takes the idea seriously, and listed among best technical talks.

wi-b9k-0KfE.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog tears down a fake Apple A1265 USB charger and shows the shortcuts that make it unsafe, such as poor isolation.
wi-b9k-0KfE.why: HN points to it as an engineer's evidence of why cheap counterfeit chargers are dangerous.

wrHXA2cSpNU.summary: Deepfake artist Shamook's improved version of the Luke Skywalker scene from The Mandalorian season 2 finale, replacing the official CGI face with a deepfake.
wrHXA2cSpNU.why: HN cites it as an example of deepfakes producing a more convincing CGI human than the studio's own effort.

ww47bR86wSc.summary: An animated Sprouts video presenting Dietrich Bonhoeffer's argument that stupidity is more dangerous than evil, because reason cannot reach stupid people. It frames stupidity as a social and moral phenomenon.
ww47bR86wSc.why: HN commenters cite it when discussing Bonhoeffer's idea that stupidity is a moral failing rather than an intellectual one.

wymmCdLdPvM.summary: Numberphile with Tim Browning on the sum-of-three-cubes problem and why 33 was the lowest unsolved case. The description notes a later solution for 33.
wymmCdLdPvM.why: Linked in threads on sums of cubes and Diophantine equations as an accessible introduction.

w-CGSQAO5-Q.summary: Toyota Research Institute presents an approach for teaching robots new dexterous behaviors from human demonstration. It explains why this capability matters and what advances made it possible.
w-CGSQAO5-Q.why: HN commenters point to it as evidence that robots can already learn manipulation tasks quickly, using diffusion-based policies.

w2itwFJCgFQ.summary: In a TEDGlobal talk, Raffaello D'Andrea demonstrates quadcopters that play catch, balance, learn and coordinate, using algorithms that treat them like athletes. It includes Kinect-controlled quads.
w2itwFJCgFQ.why: HN cites it for the live demo of multicopters flying with fewer working rotors.

w4sLAQvEH-M.summary: Veritasium visits Richard Lenski's lab to explain the decades-long E. coli evolution experiment, which asks how repeatable evolution is and shows bacteria evolving to use a new food source.
w4sLAQvEH-M.why: Linked as the go-to overview of the long-running bacteria experiment whenever real-time evolution or resistance comes up.

wCDIYvFmgW8.summary: The restored 4k official music video for Fatboy Slim's Weapon of Choice featuring Bootsy Collins, directed by Spike Jonze, with Christopher Walken dancing around a hotel lobby. It won multiple MTV awards and a Grammy.
wCDIYvFmgW8.why: HN mentions it mostly in passing as a joke or trivia, such as noting that Spike Jonze appears as a dancer.

wCrtk-pyP0I.summary: Veritasium explains why a halved grape in a microwave makes plasma: the grape traps microwaves, and the fields of two halves interact to concentrate energy where they touch.
wCrtk-pyP0I.why: Mentioned as a classic physics demo in threads on microwaves and related resonance effects.

wCzS2FZoB-I.summary: A short Insider Tech video on New Story and ICON building 3D-printed homes that can go up in under 24 hours for around $4,000. It frames the effort as a way to address global homelessness.
wCzS2FZoB-I.why: Cited as a concrete example that 3D-printed houses already exist and are cheap.

wE3fmFTtP9g.summary: Boston Dynamics shows WildCat, a four-legged robot built with DARPA funding that reached about 19 mph using bounding and galloping gaits.
wE3fmFTtP9g.why: Used as a reference point when comparing other legged robots, such as the MIT Cheetah, on gait and speed.

wKDdLWAdcbM.summary: A one-minute clip from Yes Minister in which Sir Humphrey explains the role of a civil servant, listing the contradictory policies he has loyally served across eleven governments.
wKDdLWAdcbM.why: HN posts it as a joke about bureaucrats and institutional conformity.

wO61D9x6lNY.summary: A 21-minute animation showing how a sphere can be turned inside out without creases or tears, known as sphere eversion.
wO61D9x6lNY.why: Linked as a classic visualization when sphere eversion or counterintuitive mathematics comes up.

wORv8J1n0y8.summary: A two-minute promotional video introducing the team at Memrise, a language-learning company, as part of their recruiting page.
wORv8J1n0y8.why: It is only linked from Memrise's monthly Who is Hiring posts as a recruiting video.

wPiLLplofYw.summary: An old lab video of a decerebrate cat walking on a treadmill and shifting between gait patterns as the speed changes. It is used to illustrate that much locomotion control comes from the spinal cord and body mechanics rather than the brain.
wPiLLplofYw.why: Used as a vivid example of spinal pattern generators and morphological control in locomotion discussions.

wPrUmViN_5c.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1995 film Hackers in which characters trade technobabble about RISC architecture changing everything.
wPrUmViN_5c.why: Used as a running joke whenever RISC, RISC-V or processor architecture comes up.

wRnSnfiUI54.summary: The mostly unmodified clip from Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan in which Kirk screams 'Khaaan!'
wRnSnfiUI54.why: Used as the source of the famous scream, either as a joke or as the reference for Khan-themed projects.

wSIWpFPkYrk.summary: A spoof commercial by the Groen Brothers for a Star Wars-style laser defense system against mosquitoes.
wSIWpFPkYrk.why: Posted as a joke whenever laser anti-mosquito devices come up, as an early internet gem.

w_rKA6ROAVk.summary: A short recruitment video for the Newport Beach Police Department promoting its jobs and pay.
w_rKA6ROAVk.why: Cited critically in policing threads as evidence of what kind of recruits and culture police departments seek.

whbyuy2nHBg.summary: Chinese Cooking Demystified shows an ordinary, everyday Chinese wet market to counter sensationalized coverage during the early pandemic, with a pinned comment adding nuance.
whbyuy2nHBg.why: Linked to show that typical wet markets are ordinary, grocery-store-like places, not the exotic scenes often portrayed.

wmVkJvieaOA.summary: Innuendo Studios' video essay in the Alt-Right Playbook series argues that bad-faith actors force opponents to defend their positions, so the way to avoid their trap is to never play defense.
wmVkJvieaOA.why: HN cites it when arguing that debating bad-faith arguers hands them the framing and exposure.

wmin5WkOuPw.summary: The official music video for Firestarter by The Prodigy, the 1990s electronic hit featuring Keith Flint.
wmin5WkOuPw.why: HN mentions it mainly as nostalgia, a tribute to Keith Flint, or a throwaway joke rather than as a recommendation.

wpIJVWXsBBI.summary: ITS Tactical demonstrates how a ballpoint pen can open a zippered suitcase without leaving a trace, bypassing its lock, and suggests countermeasures.
wpIJVWXsBBI.why: Cited in TSA luggage-lock threads to show that locks on zippered bags offer little real security.

wsixsRI-Sz4.summary: Kara Swisher and Walt Mossberg interview Elon Musk at Code Conference 2016 about one-way Mars missions, electric vehicles, autonomous cars, SpaceX booster reuse and AI.
wsixsRI-Sz4.why: Mostly cited as a dated source for Musk's past claims, such as autonomous driving being essentially solved, and his rocket reuse analogies.

wv9n9Casp1o.summary: Footage of DC-X Flight 8 from July 1995 at White Sands, in which the Delta Clipper Experimental reusable rocket turned over into a re-entry profile and re-oriented itself for landing.
wv9n9Casp1o.why: HN cites it as proof that vertical-landing reusable rockets were flown decades before SpaceX, including the same hover-slam landing.

wvhW8cp15tk.summary: The 2007 D5 conference joint interview of Steve Jobs and Bill Gates, hosted by Walt Mossberg and Kara Swisher, discussing the history of Apple and Microsoft, partnership, competition and computing's future.
wvhW8cp15tk.why: Cited for specific Jobs and Gates remarks, such as how the two companies helped each other and how Apple recovered, though one commenter notes it was widely derided as an interview.

wzkAeopX7P0.summary: A short demonstration of radioteletype (RTTY), a digital communication mode used in amateur radio, showing what the signal sounds like.
wzkAeopX7P0.why: HN commenters link it as a sound sample when discussing data-over-audio projects that resemble RTTY.
